findings.asked: Evaluate expressions with zero, negative and other indices.
findings.wentWrong: x to the zero was given as 3 or 0; a negative index produced -8; another produced -1000 or -30; a letter crept into a numerical answer.
findings.rule: Zero index = 1; negative index = reciprocal, always positive.

findings.wentWrong: Most managed 0, many -1, only the better candidates -3.
findings.rule: a to the minus 3 = 1 / a cubed.

findings.wentWrong: About a third gave 8; the majority gave 2, having taken the root but not applied the power.
findings.rule: Root first, then raise to the power - both steps.

findings.wentWrong: One in ten gave 3 instead of 8.
findings.rule: a to the m/n = (n-th root of a) to the m.

findings.wentWrong: Common wrong answers 2 and 4; only a small number reached 8.
findings.rule: Write the root step and the power step separately.

findings.asked: Simplify algebraic indices; prove a numerical index statement.
findings.wentWrong: Over half did not demonstrate what the indices mean in the proof.
findings.rule: In a proof, rewrite each number as a power of the same base.

ruleToRemember: a to the 0 = 1; a to the -n = 1 / a to the n (positive); a to the m/n = (n-th root of a) to the m - do the root and the power; in proofs express everything as powers of one base.
aStarSignal: Setting up and solving simultaneous equations from index laws, or proving an index identity by matching bases.
